source: GitHub (MiSTer-devel/WonderSwan_MiSTer issue #10, 'How to convert saves for use in software emulators?', comment of 2022-03-29, attachment added in an edit)
author: euan-forrester (savefileconverter.com author): 'I'm using the emulator mednafen, the default for OpenEmu' ... 'I made a save with mednafen for Rockman & Forte where the first slot has the first level passed'
licence: none stated (a file attached to a public GitHub issue)
what_it_is: euan-forrester's own save, slot 1 with the first level cleared. 32768 bytes of cartridge SRAM (the size Mednafen gives header RAM type 0x02), no header or footer; named the Mednafen way, <ROM name>.<game MD5>.sav (filesys.fname_sav default '%f.%M%x'). 523004d48e9d606e1557c2c57af6790b is the MD5 of the No-Intro ROM.
note: Emulator stated by the author; the frontend is inferred from 'the default for OpenEmu', and OpenEmu's Mednafen core keeps Mednafen's default fname_sav, so standalone Mednafen would write the same name and bytes. Caveat: the zip's __MACOSX AppleDouble entry records kMDItemWhereFroms http://localhost:8080/ and a Chrome quarantine stamp of 2022-03-29 16:18 UTC, so the attached copy was downloaded from the author's local savefileconverter dev server; for WonderSwan that tool only adds or strips 0x200 bytes at the end, so the 32 KiB are not expected to have changed. The zip also holds that __MACOSX/._ file (412 bytes), not copied here. Zip entry dated 2022-03-29 09:31.
